OmaStats 1.5 keeps your disk and sensor choices on the same hardware across reboots, and makes settings changes stick when the machine is busy.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.5.0/omastats-v1.5.0.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![The same drive stays selected when the kernel swaps nvme0n1 and nvme1n1 between boots, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.5.0/omastats-1.5.0-disk-identity-dark.png)

## New

- **Disk choices follow the drive.** The kernel names NVMe drives in the order their controllers come up, so `nvme0n1` can be a different drive after a reboot, and a disk readout could jump to the other one. Disks are now saved by their `/dev/disk/by-id` name, built from the model and serial, and stay with the same drive. Choices saved by kernel name are switched to the drive's id automatically. By @crmne.
- **Sensors keep their drive or DIMM.** Two NVMe drives, or two memory modules, used to share one sensor id, so picking one could show the other. Sensors that share a driver now include the device's PCI or I2C address, and "NVMe 1" and "NVMe 2" are numbered by that address instead of probe order. By @crmne.

## Fixed

- **Settings changes stick under load.** While plugins load, the shell can replace the config copy it gives each plugin, and the widget kept the old copy, which never updated. On a busy machine that happened often: a change could be undone, take a long time to show, or bring back old values for other settings. OmaStats now checks its settings against `shell.json` itself. By @crmne.
- **A new refresh interval applies at once.** The sampler used to finish its current interval first, so switching from 10 s to 1 s could take ten seconds. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- Version 1.4.1 and earlier can't read a disk saved by id. If you go back to an older version, choose the disk again in Settings.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/crmne/omastats/compare/v1.4.1...v1.5.0
